edges_to_update.reasoning: While no direct target engagement biomarkers were reported, both nivolumab (PD-1) and ipilimumab (CTLA-4) are established checkpoint inhibitors with well-characterized binding profiles. The drugs were administered at standard doses over adequate duration.

The combination failed to improve outcomes over nivolumab monotherapy in adjuvant melanoma (RFS HR 0.90, not significant), suggesting that dual checkpoint blockade may not provide additional biological benefit in this setting compared to PD-1 blockade alone.

RFS is a well-established endpoint for adjuvant melanoma therapy and is accepted by regulators as a meaningful clinical benefit measure. The endpoint was appropriately measured and reported with adequate follow-up duration.

PD-L1 <1% subgroup showed numerical benefit with longer median RFS (33.18 vs 25.33 months) and HR 0.92, suggesting potential differential response in low PD-L1 expressing tumors, though not statistically significant.
